correctness.rationale: For m>=4 degrees m,3,2 separate hub, spoke attachments and sector interiors after one round; further 1-WL rounds propagate color information inward by distance from equally colored sector endpoints, one layer each step, with final split at floor(n/2). For m=3 the hub shares degree 3 with spoke vertices at round one, but neighbor-degree multisets separate them at round two; sector distance propagation remains unaffected. Dihedral rotations/reflections across the identical m paths put precisely vertices of the same nearest-spoke distance in one orbit, and the color classes separate all other orbit types. Independently implemented one-WL and orbit formulas and checked n=2..18 and m=3..12 (170 pairs), including small n and m=3 boundaries. This finite check is supporting evidence for the all-parameter inductive distance-wave argument.

value.rationale: Jahangir graphs form a standard well-studied infinite family. Stabilization round depth and whether 1-WL detects every automorphism orbit are natural computational graph invariants, and this theorem determines both exactly for all permitted parameters. The m=3 hub/spoke degree-collision introduces a genuine sharp structural exception; more than a finite table or a relabeling of generic universal-cover bounds.

final_claim: For standard Jahangir graph J_(n,m), n>=2 and m>=3, 1-dimensional color-refinement stabilization from uniform coloring is floor(n/2) for m>=4 and max(2,floor(n/2)) for m=3, and its stable equitable partition equals the automorphism-orbit partition.
limitations: Only ordinary 1-WL from uniform coloring on equally spaced spoke Jahangir graphs n>=2,m>=3; no irregular wheel or 2-WL claim.
Some older named-family literature was available only at metadata/abstract level; no whole-document negative coverage inferred.
